sources.tapDrills: Machinery's Handbook, 31st ed.; ASME B1.1 (Unified), ASME B1.13M (metric)
sources.rollTapDrills: Form tap formula at 65% thread (OSG / Emuge form tap guidance); supplier tables are authoritative
sources.drillSizes: ASME B94.11M number and letter drill sizes; fractions exact
sources.npt: ASME B1.20.1 sizes; tap drills without reaming per Tapco pipe tap chart (OSG agrees)
sources.cuttingSpeeds: HSS bands: https://littlemachineshop.com/pages/cutting-speeds; carbide milling SFM and chip loads: https://www.lakeshorecarbide.com/pdf/GENERAL%20PURPOSE%20EM%20SPECS.pdf; turning carbide and feed per rev are conservative JobLine estimates (machining-core 1.0.0)

cuttingSpeeds.note: Use sharp, polished edges and reliable chip evacuation.
Higher strength than 6061; monitor chip adhesion.
Low-carbon steel can form a built-up edge.
Heat treatment changes cutting behavior substantially.
HSS reference family includes resulfurized grades; ordinary 4140 may cut less freely. Verify tooling data.
Carbide is preferred. Check actual hardness on the material certificate.
Work-hardens; avoid dwelling or rubbing. Maintain a positive cut.
HSS speeds are estimates (316 is not in the published austenitic row). Tough chips and work hardening demand consistent engagement.
Not suitable for hardened A2. Hardened tooling requires supplier-specific data.
Abrasive material; control dust. Dry-cut adjustment is not applied to cast iron.
Use brass-compatible geometry; aggressive rake can grab.
